title: 'Cap 278 signing off': Ajinkya Rahane retires from international cricket
content: Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane has announced his retirement from international cricket. He shared this news through a video message posted on his Instagram account. Rahane represented India in all three formats during his extensive international career. He played 85 Test matches, 90 ODIs, and 20 T20Is for the country. Rahane was also part of India's historic Test series win in Australia in 2020-21.

content: TOI understands that Bumrah will begin gradually increasing his bowling workload after suffering an impact injury during the ODI series in England, while Gill has sought help from specialists outside the BCCI for his chronic neck problem.

CEO Andy Jassy views artificial intelligence as a major opportunity.  Amazon plans substantial capital expenditure for AI infrastructure in upcoming years.  This investment reflects a strategy to avoid missing a key technological shift.

title: Ukraine loses F-16 during combat operations against Russian attacks
content: Ukraine's Air Force confirmed an F-16 fighter jet loss during a combat mission.  The pilot ejected safely, and investigators are examining the crash site.  This incident adds to previous F-16 losses since their Ukrainian service entry.  Ukraine's air defense faces challenges with interceptor shortages and Russian missile production.  Sustained allied support remains crucial for Ukraine's defense capabilities.

title: 'Embarrassing': Ex-captain slams India's blue being replaced by saffron
content: Former India hockey captain Viren Rasquinha criticised Hockey India’s decision to replace the team’s iconic blue jersey with saffron ahead of the 2026 Hockey World Cup, calling it "embarrassing" and questioning the change. Hockey India said the new colour symbolises "courage, sacrifice & victory" and represents new beginnings. India’s men and women will begin their World Cup campaigns in Group D.

title: 'BJP fears losing': Prashant Kishor alleges supporters 'picked up' before bypoll
content: Prashant Kishor alleged Bihar Police detained his supporters before the Bankipur bypoll. He claimed the ruling BJP fears losing the assembly seat and orchestrated these detentions. Kishor stated police could not reveal the whereabouts of over sixteen detained supporters. He further alleged the BJP used administrative machinery and a fake video to influence voters. The Jan Suraaj Party founder vowed action against erring police officials after the bypoll.

title: Kevin O'Leary says China's rise will unite US, Canada and Mexico
content: Kevin O'Leary suggests China's growing power will unite North American economies.  Canada offers minerals and energy, while the US provides scale and innovation.  Mexico also plays a vital role in the regional economic landscape.  Companies are increasingly using cheaper Chinese artificial intelligence models.  This shift occurs as the race for technological dominance accelerates globally.

title: Musk's million-dollar plan to rescue Trump in mid-elections
content: Elon Musk is reviving his political action committee, America PAC, for the 2026 elections. This group previously spent over $260 million to support Donald Trump's 2024 campaign. America PAC will now focus on increasing Republican voter turnout through various outreach methods. The organization plans to collaborate with other Republican groups to boost their efforts. Musk's involvement signals a significant financial push for the GOP's midterm goals.

title: 750 Indian girls failed at school experiments; their satellite now orbits Earth
content: After overcoming an initial setback, Indian schoolgirls have successfully launched their AzaadiSAT satellite into orbit. This remarkable project engaged 750 students from 75 schools throughout India, where they contributed to building satellite components that were incorporated into a real ISRO satellite. This successful launch represents a significant stride toward inspiring girls in STEM education, showcasing their dedication and resilience in the face of challenges.

title: Remora hitches 19-minute ride as sea turtle lays eggs in Costa Rica
content: On a picturesque Costa Rican beach, an unexpected sight caught the eyes of researchers when a mother sea turtle arrived with a lively suckerfish clinging to her shell for an astonishing nineteen minutes. The fish, which seemed to adapt momentarily to land, showcased its gill movements. After careful observation, it was returned to its aquatic home, darting away with unexpected vigor, leaving onlookers astonished by its resilience.

title: Zuckerberg's 1,000-plus words open letter shows Apple's iPhone change still hurts Meta
content: Mark Zuckerberg's 1,000-word Wall Street Journal op-ed on superintelligence reads like philosophy, but its argument against concentrated power traces back to one Apple change. iOS 14.5's App Tracking Transparency cost Meta roughly $10 billion and triggered a 26.4% stock crash that erased $232 billion. Five years on, Meta's open-weight Llama strategy and AI spending are shaped by that lesson in platform control.

title: Microsoft Q4 results: Azure tops $100 bn as AI growth helps beat earnings estimates
content: Microsoft reported strong cloud revenue growth and increased paid AI users.  Azure revenue surpassed one hundred billion dollars for the first time.  Microsoft 365 Copilot now has over thirty million paid seats.  Investors are observing returns from significant artificial intelligence spending.  The company's shares saw a notable increase after the earnings announcement.

title: 'Clicky Ponting' cheating row: Saltburn Cricket Club suspends player
content: Saltburn Cricket Club have suspended a player nicknamed "Clicky Ponting" after he was accused of clicking his fingers to fake an edge during a local league match in England. The viral incident, viewed over 7.5 million times on X, sparked widespread criticism. The club said it is fully cooperating with the investigation, while the player remains suspended pending its outcome.

title: Mental disorder alone cannot be a ground for divorce, Jharkhand HC rules
content: The Jharkhand high court ruled mental disorder alone is insufficient for divorce. A spouse must prove the illness prevents reasonable cohabitation. The court dismissed a husband's appeal for divorce based on his wife's alleged mental illness. He failed to provide medical evidence or expert testimony to support his claims. The court upheld the family court's decision refusing to dissolve the marriage.

title: 'Answer now': CJP invokes Rahul's claims, questions Shah over July 20 action
content: The Cockroach Janta Party demanded answers from Union Home Minister Amit Shah.  Rahul Gandhi alleged Shah ordered police action against student protesters on July twenty.  Gandhi claimed Shah is either culpable or incompetent regarding the incident.  The BJP rejected these allegations, calling them false claims.  The exchange occurs amid ongoing political debate over the protest.

title: Three firefighters killed as deadly wildfires rage across southern Europe
content: Greece's fire department said the firefighters lost their lives while tackling separate fires on the island of Crete and in the country's southern mainland. The deaths came as soaring temperatures and strong winds made firefighting operations increasingly difficult. The wildfires now stretch across a vast area from the Atlantic coast to the eastern Mediterranean, affecting countries including France, Spain, Greece and Turkey.

title: India’s retail leasing jumps 20% in H1 2026 as fashion brands lead expansion
content: In early 2026, India's retail leasing market experienced a remarkable growth of twenty percent, driven primarily by retailer expansion and new property developments. The fashion and apparel sectors emerged as the leaders in leasing activities, closely followed by food and beverage markets. Most leasing actions were led by domestic retailers and direct-to-consumer brands, while institutional investment in organized retail real estate is slated to remain robust.

title: E20 may harm rubber parts of vehicles manufactured between 2005-16: Nitin Gadkari
content: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari informed Rajya Sabha about E20 fuel impacts. Studies found no major performance impact on overall vehicle operations. BS-VI vehicles continue meeting emission norms when tested with E20 fuel. Legacy vehicles did not exhibit significant performance variations or abnormal wear. However, some BS-III vehicles may require rubber part replacements.

title: Mumbai man, suffering stroke, kept at police station for hours over 'drunk driving'
content: A 73-year-old man suffered a stroke while driving his car last week. Police detained him for five hours on suspicion of drunk driving. This delay prevented him from receiving timely medical treatment for his stroke. He was subsequently left partially paralyzed and remains in the ICU. His family claims police ignored stroke symptoms and proceeded with FIR.

title: The Republic of discontent: Seven decades of student revolt in India
content: From a food riot in Calcutta to a satirical cockroach party that just cost a minister his job, India’s students have spent seven decades proving they are the country’s most unpredictable political force.

title: 'Let someone else do PM's tasks': CJP's Dipke says 'Modi good as influencer'
content: Abhijeet Dipke returned to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar after a student protest at Jantar Mantar. He warned the central government about continued student anger and potential future actions. Dipke alleged students faced harassment and intimidation instead of government dialogue. He criticized the Prime Minister and questioned the effectiveness of new laws. The student leader vowed to launch a larger agitation if necessary.

title: How India became the world's worst doping offender: A crisis threatening sports
content: According to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s (WADA) 2024 Testing Figures Report, released in Dec 2025, India registered 260 adverse analytical findings (AAFs) from 7,113 samples collected during the year — a positivity rate of 3.6%. Among countries conducting more than 5,000 tests annually, India recorded the highest positivity rate in the world for the third consecutive year.

title: Samsung Q2 results: Tech giant posts record high $62 billion profit on AI chip boom
content: Samsung Electronics achieved its highest-ever quarterly operating profit, fueled by strong AI chip demand.  Rival SK Hynix also reported record revenue, reflecting industry strength.  However, investor sentiment declined due to expansion plans and Chinese competition.  Both companies are investing heavily in new chipmaking facilities and data centers.  Global partnerships are strengthening to secure memory chip supplies for AI.

The officer was previously arrested and sent to judicial remand for fourteen days.  The woman IPS trainee had lodged her complaint eleven days prior to the arrest.  The case involves allegations of sexual misconduct and privacy violations at SVPNPA.

title: Record alert: Indian boxers eclipse Birmingham tally with 10 guaranteed medals

title: 11-year-old's SoilShade balls earn spot in $25,000 science contest
content: An 11-year-old Florida student has reached the finals of a national science competition.  Her innovative soilshade balls help farmers conserve water during dry weather conditions.  This eco-friendly invention slows evaporation and keeps soil moist for extended periods.  She will compete for a $25,000 prize and mentorship from 3M scientists.  The competition celebrates young innovators using STEM to solve real-world problems.

title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
content: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. This trend signals a significant cultural shift toward cooling solutions. Manufacturers report double-digit growth in sales across several European countries. Rising temperatures and extreme heat events are becoming impossible to ignore. This shift is driven by comfort and the growing recognition of heat as a public health risk.

title: Honeymoon murder: Sonam Raghuvanshi surrenders after SC cancels bail
content: Sonam Raghuvanshi surrendered before a Shillong court following a Supreme Court order.  Her bail was cancelled by the apex court, directing her immediate surrender.  She is accused of conspiring to murder her husband during their honeymoon last year.  Raja Raghuvanshi's body was discovered in a gorge after the couple went missing.  The accused was remanded to judicial custody after her surrender to authorities.

title: Kirti Kulhari loses Rs 2.4 lakh to cyber fraud, files complaint with Mumbai police
content: In a shocking turn of events, Kirti Kulhari, the talented actress, encountered cyber fraud in Mumbai. Unidentified criminals infiltrated her mobile phone and credit card, executing unauthorized transactions that totaled Rs 243,852 in mere minutes. Disturbed by this breach, Kulhari promptly reported the incident to the police, prompting the Cyber Cell to launch an investigation. The incident happened while she enjoyed a show at a theatre in Andheri West.

title: Salman Rushdie stabbing: Attacker convicted on Hezbollah support, terror charges
content: A US man already serving a lengthy sentence was convicted on new federal charges.  He was found guilty of providing material support to the militant group Hezbollah.  Prosecutors linked his actions to a 1989 fatwa and a later speech.  The author Salman Rushdie testified during the federal trial about the attack.  This conviction adds to his existing sentence for attempted murder.

title: Crude prices retreat as oil continues flowing through Hormuz alternatives
content: Oil prices declined on Thursday after a significant rally the previous day. Crude oil continued to move out of the Middle East despite escalating conflict. Shipping activity indicated that oil supplies were still finding routes out of the region. Military actions intensified with US-Saudi strikes targeting Iran-backed forces in Iraq. Saudi Arabia is reportedly assembling a coalition to protect Red Sea shipping from Houthi attacks.

title: We are in India, be realistic, says HC, lifts curbs on hotel over 2 insects
content: The Bombay high court quashed a hotel's license suspension after finding minor hygiene issues.  A solitary finding of two insects did not justify the continued suspension of the license.  The court accepted the hotel's undertaking to maintain high sanitation standards.  The Food and Drug Administration's drive aims to improve food safety across Maharashtra.  The court appreciated the state and FDA actions in enforcing food safety laws.

title: Former CSK coach tipped for England's Test head coach role
content: Stephen Fleming is reportedly the frontrunner for England's Test head coach position. He has emerged as the preferred candidate after a thorough interview process. Fleming will replace Brendon McCullum, who is now leading England's white-ball teams. Fleming recently concluded a successful eighteen-year tenure with Chennai Super Kings. Joe Root will temporarily lead the team before Fleming's official start.

title: 2 years after death, SC clears ex-PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
content: The Supreme Court has cleared former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in a coal block scam case. This decision comes more than eleven years after a Delhi court summoned him as an accused. The court closed the case nearly two years after his demise in November 2024. The apex court quashed the trial court's order taking cognisance of the crime.

title: CWG: Sreeshankar wins long jump silver; Gavit claims Games record gold
content: Sreeshankar continued his impressive run at the Commonwealth Games by winning silver in the men's long jump with a best effort of 8.09m. He had also finished second at the 2022 Games, becoming the first Indian to win back-to-back Commonwealth Games medals in the event.

title: IIT-B alumnus Aphale named Ram temple trust’s first secretary, will oversee transactions
content: Jagdish Aphale, an IIT Bombay alumnus, has been appointed the Ayodhya Ram temple trust's first secretary. He will also serve as a joint signatory for financial transactions, enhancing accountability. This appointment follows recent resignations and alleged donation theft issues. Aphale previously supervised construction at the temple complex for nearly four years. His integration into the trust's internal processes has been ongoing for two weeks.

title: DGCA-ordered probe cleared Dreamliner fuel switch: Government
content: A Boeing probe found no abnormality in the B787 fuel control switch locking mechanism. This examination was ordered by the DGCA after a crew reported an issue post-landing. The switches control fuel supply and have faced scrutiny after a past crash incident. Further inspection of the complete thrust control module at the OEM facility is currently underway.

title: Denied seat, student hacks IIT-Kanpur website to show his 'merit'
content: A BTech applicant hacked IIT Kanpur's website seeking admission consideration. He claimed he was denied a fair chance in the selection process. The IIT director invited the candidate to campus for an assessment. He stressed that hacking was not the correct approach to gain entry. The institute will consider him if genuine talent is demonstrated.

title: 'Not going to let him get away': Rahul targets Shah over police action on NEET protesters

Gandhi also blamed the RSS for the education sector's current problems.  Government ministers challenged Gandhi to provide proof or issue an apology.  The Lok Sabha experienced disruptions over these serious allegations.

title: Need to reinvent ways to deal with global challenges: Finance ministry
content: India's economy shows resilience despite global challenges and uncertainties.  Swift policy responses and implementation are crucial for attracting investment.  Rising crude oil prices pose a potential pressure on fiscal and current accounts.  The external sector remains resilient due to strong exports and remittances.  Adverse weather conditions present a risk to farm output and rural demand.
